entries.title: Canada welcomes EU proposal to become 'associate member'
entries.snippet: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a Canada-EU alliance would create a "beacon for other democracies".

entries.title: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
entries.snippet: South Africa police have cautioned against assuming that all the killings are linked but many women are afraid.

entries.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
entries.snippet: The US has not acknowledged carrying out February's deadly strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.

entries.title: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
entries.snippet: The BBC understands Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi are among the delegates allowed to enter the US.

entries.title: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
entries.snippet: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.

entries.title: Hyrox athlete apologises for continuing race after soiling herself
entries.snippet: Joanna Wietrzyk has also forfeited her win in the fitness competition after competing last week.

entries.title: Aztec document goes on display in Mexico after 186 years abroad
entries.snippet: France's national library is lending the manuscript recounting the history of the Aztecs to Mexico.

entries.title: Assad regime planned US journalist's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds
entries.snippet: Austin Tice’s abduction was approved by Syria’s former leader Bashar al-Assad, a source claims.

entries.title: EU announces plan to restrict social media access for under-15s
entries.snippet: Under the plans, only children over 15 would be able to set up their own social media accounts.

entries.title: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
entries.snippet: Mustafa Suleyman says he believes rival AI firm Anthropic is in effect teaching Claude it "may be conscious".

entries.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after election loss
entries.snippet: Left-wing opposition parties led by Magdalena Andersson look set to form the next government.

entries.title: Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections
entries.snippet: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

entries.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
entries.snippet: Rates were hiked in a unanimous decision despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for a cut.

entries.title: Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds
entries.snippet: The body of veteran broadcaster Owen Ndlovu was found hours after armed men kidnapped him near Johannesburg.

entries.title: One dead after torrential rain and flash floods hit Barcelona region
entries.snippet: Flooding has caused widespread disruption across Valencia and Catalonia in north-east Spain.

entries.title: River home to 500 crocodiles chosen as Olympic rowing venue
entries.snippet: A river that is home to about 500 saltwater crocodiles is given the OK to host Olympic and Paralympic rowing and canoeing events at the 2032 Brisbane Games.

entries.title: India faces 100% tariff threat over Russian oil after US House vote
entries.snippet: Trump’s tariff threat puts India’s Russian oil strategy- and its access to the US market - in a new bind.

entries.title: International students, 'visa hoppers' and backpackers targeted in Australia migration crackdown
entries.snippet: The government wants to reduce net overseas migration to 225,000 people by 2028.

entries.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
entries.snippet: A wrecked air force plane and destroyed buildings are among the images obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News.

entries.title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC
entries.snippet: Evan Spiegel says it would be "an important step forward for the industry" in an interview with the BBC.

entries.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
entries.snippet: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.

entries.title: ICE agent appears in Minnesota court to face charges in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant
entries.snippet: Christian Castro, a federal immigration officer, made his first court appearance in Minnesota since he was booked Wednesday into a local jail. Castro faces multiple state and federal charges in connection with a shooting during the immigration surge in Minnesota.

entries.title: Retired Olympic superstar Jessie Diggins wins her first-ever 100 mile trail race
entries.snippet: This spring Jessie Diggins retired as one of America's most successful winter Olympic athletes at age 34. She's relaxing by entering 100-mile trail running races and navigating what comes next.

entries.title: Can an AI chatbot save lives by answering texts about pregnancy?
entries.snippet: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.

entries.title: A year ago, President Trump pledged to lower Medicaid drug prices. Has that happened?
entries.snippet: The Trump administration's efforts to lower drug prices included promised changes to Medicaid. But it's still unclear which drugs will be affected. And each state has to opt in.

entries.title: 'American Scoundrel' traces Roy Cohn's playbook from McCarthyism to Trump
entries.snippet: In Kai Bird's biography of Cohn, he looks at how the lawyer taught Trump how to deny, delay, attack, sue and countersue, never admit defeat, side-step paying bills and avoid a paper trail.

entries.title: Greetings from Beijing, where baozi are worth the wait in line
entries.snippet: The popular fluffy steamed buns are filled with pork, vegetables, tofu — and in one trendy Beijing shop, chocolate and red beans.

entries.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
entries.snippet: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.

entries.title: The Fed raises interest rates. And, EU proposes Canada become an 'associate member'
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time in years. And, the European Union has proposed that Canada become its first-ever "associate member."

entries.title: Pressure on global chokepoints drives Asia's increased use of Arctic Trade Routes
entries.snippet: Asian nations began pilot voyages over a decade ago to find routes to Europe and the Middle East that were faster and less vulnerable to chokepoints. The ongoing war has added impetus to those efforts.

entries.title: WATCH: RFK Jr. speaks at conference for anti-vaccine group he founded
entries.snippet: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in President Donald Trump's White House.

entries.title: Work has stopped on system that was key to Trump effort to limit mail voting, USPS chief says
entries.snippet: The top official at the U.S. Postal Service said Thursday that the agency has stopped work on developing a controversial computer system that was central to President Donald Trump's effort to limit mail voting after the Supreme Court rejected his executive order this week.

entries.title: Man who sprayed Rep. Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months in prison
entries.snippet: The man who sprayed vinegar at Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar during a Minneapolis town hall was sentenced Thursday to 14 months in prison after reaching a deal with prosecutors.

entries.title: As AI behavior raises concerns, ex-researcher Jacob Coxon warns what may lie ahead
entries.snippet: OpenAI announced it had discovered six new instances of "concerning or unexpected" behavior by its artificial intelligence models. It follows repeated warnings about how rapid advances in AI threaten to outpace the ability to develop the tech safely. One of those warnings came fr

entries.title: T. rex had a body temperature similar to our own, study finds
entries.snippet: Using fossilized teeth, scientists have finally taken the T. rex's temperature — and it wasn't too different from our own.

entries.title: News Wrap: Judge says Kennedy Center must provide notice before making changes to building
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Thursday, a federal judge ordered that Kennedy Center officials provide a 30-day notice before making any significant physical changes to the building, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is welcoming a proposal that could see his country join the European Union

entries.title: Congress passes new sanctions on Russia and countries using Russian energy
entries.snippet: A bill to impose sweeping new sanctions on Russia, and on countries using Russian energy, is now on its way to President Trump after the House overwhelmingly passed it Wednesday night. Congress also took action this week on data centers, college sports and the Iran war. Capitol H

entries.title: How Trump's immigration crackdown made it harder to become U.S. citizen
entries.snippet: September 17 is Constitution Day, a commemoration of the founding document signed on that date in 1787. But for immigrants seeking U.S. citizenship, the path to naturalization has grown more difficult as the Trump administration has added new requirements and tightened vetting st

entries.title: Qatari spokesman on regional war and the path back to U.S.-Iran talks
entries.snippet: Violence has spread across the Middle East since the U.S. and Israel launched the war in Iran. Qatar has spent months mediating between Iran and the U.S. while also being targeted by Iranian strikes. Nick Schifrin sat down with Dr. Majed al-Ansari, adviser to Qatar's prime minist

entries.title: Trump's push to restrict mail ballots failed. Other efforts to reshape the midterms continue
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court this week closed the chapter on one of Trump's effort to dramatically overhaul of the nation's mail voting processes. But the case was just one example of the Republican president's numerous attempts to assert federal control over the upcoming midterms.

entries.title: Wheelchair tennis celebrates 50 years and a new wave of popularity
entries.snippet: Professional wheelchair tennis players are competing for their countries this week in the World Team Cup at the U.S. Tennis Association's National Campus in Orlando. It's part of the 50th anniversary of the sport's creation and comes at a time when popularity is growing. Amna Naw

entries.title: Jon Ronson and Geoff Bennett discuss modern masculinity on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: Jon Ronson's new book, "The Castle," asks questions about what young men are being taught about what it means to be a man. Ronson joined Geoff Bennett on our PBS News podcast "Settle In" and discussed why certain visions of masculinity are proving so powerful right now.

entries.title: Tens of thousands flee as Iran-backed Houthis draw Yemen into wider war
entries.snippet: An estimated 125,000 people have fled as Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced down the Red Sea coast to a key maritime chokepoint.

entries.title: Jon Kyl, long-serving lawmaker from Arizona who shaped water policy, dies at 84
entries.snippet: Kyl spent almost three decades in Congress, serving in both chambers, and watched his party undergo a drastic transformation, with his career spanning Ronald Reagan's presidency to President Donald Trump's first term.

entries.title: Judge orders Kennedy Center to provide 30 days' notice before making any major physical changes
entries.snippet: The Kennedy Center's Trump-aligned board, chaired by the president, voted to close the center after U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper blocked the institution from returning President Donald Trump's name to the building.

entries.title: Climate change made deadly Nepal glacier and rock collapse more likely, analysis finds
entries.snippet: Human-caused global warming thinned glaciers and thawed mountain permafrost, likely helping to destabilize the Himalayan slope that collapsed last month and unleashed catastrophic flooding across Nepal, according to a report released Thursday.

entries.title: About 35 million people have been put into new House districts in the fight over congressional maps, report says
entries.snippet: The findings display the stark overhaul that partisan redistricting fights kicked off by President Donald Trump last year have caused for Americans across the country.

entries.title: A global AI safety strategy depends on U.S.-China cooperation. They each see the other as the problem
entries.snippet: AI governance is expected to be on the agenda in a meeting planned for next week in Washington between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

entries.title: Florida congresswoman running for reelection breaks with Trump on immigration
entries.snippet: Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar is out with a new ad criticizing President Donald Trump's deportation campaign.

entries.title: WATCH: Jeffries calls on Republicans to stay in Washington to work on AI safety
entries.snippet: Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries blasted House Republicans for leaving Washington until the midterm elections rather than working to ensure the safety of artificial intelligence.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Trump hails 'major progress' in setting up US base in Poland
entries.snippet: The location of the permanent US military base in Poland could be announced "very soon," Donald Trump has said. The US president also praised the leadership of his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki.

entries.title: US: Trump administration weakens Endangered Species Act
entries.snippet: In a recent memo, the US government would no longer consider the unintentional killing of protected wildlife as unlawful.

entries.title: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
entries.snippet: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

entries.title: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
entries.snippet: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

entries.title: Germany: Third malaria death linked to Frankfurt Airport
entries.snippet: Two new malaria cases have been registered this week near Frankfurt airport, two months after cases first emerged.

entries.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
entries.snippet: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia, Houthis exchange blows as conflict escalates
entries.snippet: Five people were reportedly killed as the escalation between the two sides continues to spiral. The Houthis denied attacking Mecca, with Saudi Arabia saying one person was killed by drone shrapnel.

entries.title: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
entries.snippet: German judges and prosecutors warn that the coalition needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

entries.title: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
entries.snippet: The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

entries.title: Smuggling suspected as more rare animals seen in India
entries.snippet: Orangutans, rare reptiles and other exotic animals are popping up in India, suggesting the country is becoming a major destination for trafficked wildlife.

entries.title: Fact check: How disinformation fuels Houthi-Saudi conflict
entries.snippet: As fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates, old and repurposed videos have flooded social media, with many presented as fresh footage from the front lines.

entries.title: South Africa: Police find 9th body of woman amid spree fears
entries.snippet: Police in South Africa have discovered the bodies of nine women east of Johannesburg in two months, stoking fears of a serial killer or group of killers.

entries.title: Europe seeks stricter age limits for TikTok, Instagram and Facebook
entries.snippet: The European Commission wants to bar children under 13 from social media platforms and curb addictive features such as infinite scrolling. Companies that fail to comply could face hefty fines.

entries.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
entries.snippet: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

entries.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
entries.snippet: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

entries.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
entries.snippet: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

entries.title: Canada's Carney welcomes associate status idea in EU speech
entries.snippet: Mark Carney wants to strengthen Canada's ties to the European Union amid a growing rift with the US under Donald Trump. The US president has threatened to halt trade with Europe if it makes Canada an associate EU member.

entries.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
entries.snippet: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

entries.title: Fiji declares HIV a national crisis, 1 in 60 adults carry it
entries.snippet: Fiji's government estimates that HIV prevalence has almost tripled in the last five years. It's expanding testing, prevention and treatment services. In 2025 the tiny island recorded 16 times more new cases than in 2019.
